text:
leo: quick idea — open to feedback: propose a thin, language-agnostic Call abstraction for SDKs that separates transport, retry policy, and pagination semantics. aim is: single mental model across py/ts/go so product teams can reason about behavior consistently. will sketch shapes below.
maria: high level sounds good. can you clarify what 'thin' means here vs current rich client helpers?
leo: thin = surface just enough to express "unary vs streaming" + idempotency hint + pagination cursor shape. helpers live on top in each language. prevents duplicated retry logic spread across helpers.
sam: concern: error types differ a lot across runtimes. how would we map transport errors -> retryable vs non-retryable?
leo: plan is to have a small enum: RETRYABLE, NON_RETRYABLE, TRANSIENT_BACKOFF, and a canonical error classifier in the core runtime. SDKs map native errors into that classifier. keeps retry policy language-neutral.
anya: can we see a pseudo-shape?
leo: sure, rough sketch:```ts
// language-agnostic pseudo
interface CallOptions {
  mode: 'unary' | 'server_stream' | 'client_stream' | 'bidi',
  idempotency?: 'idempotent' | 'non-idempotent' | 'unknown',
  pager?: {cursorKey?: string, pageSizeKey?: string},
  retryPolicy?: string // ref to named policy
}
```

maria: i like named policies. we should surface a default per-route (cheap default) and let libs override.
sam: pagination: how do we avoid leaking transport details (e.g., page tokens vs cursor ids) into core?
leo: core only exposes an opaque cursor string and a small helper to merge results. language helpers unwrap common transports (rest/grpc) into that opaque cursor. goal: SDKs provide ergonomic iterators that use the Call abstraction underneath.
anya: fallback behavior: when a call fails mid-page, do we retry the whole page or resume? that affects idempotency model.
leo: default: for non-idempotent calls we do no automatic resume; surface partial results and let caller decide. for idempotent calls we can retry individual pages if server supports stateless cursors. we document fallbacks clearly.
ci-bot: note: related RFC PR #789 updated build matrix; running tests. :gear:
maria: telemetry — we need consistent de-dup keys to correlate retries across languages for cost analysis. include a trace_id in CallOptions by default?
sam: +1 trace_id. also expose attempt metadata in iterator yields so application can decide to re-run logic or dedupe.
leo: implementation plan: 1) thin Call spec + err classifier 2) small shim in runtime to map transport errors 3) proof-of-concept in python SDK only (PR for shape) 4) iterate on TS/Go shims once py usage looks clean.
anya: timeline?
leo: PoC PR this week, docs + examples next week, sync with platform infra to add canonical classifier mapping.
maria: one more tradeoff: complexity on language side vs fewer bugs. i support moving classifier to runtime to reduce per-sdk variance.
sam: agree. will review PoC. any objections to named retry policies as strings vs typed objects? typed objects are nicer but harder to keep consistent across langs. strings + central registry seems pragmatic.
leo: noted. thanks all — i'll post the PoC link when ready and tag reviewers. :thumbsup:
